arxiv-2201-02292.title: Unconditional Effects of General Policy Interventions Thanks: For helpful conversations, we thank Javier Alejo, George Bulman, and Augusto Nieto-Barthaburu. All errors remain our own. This paper supersedes Location-Scale and Compensated Effects in Unconditional Quantile Regressions .
arxiv-2201-02292.creator: Julián Martínez-Iriarte, Gabriel Montes-Rojas, Yixiao Sun
arxiv-2201-02292.description: Abstract This paper studies the unconditional effects of a general policy intervention, which includes location-scale shifts and simultaneous shifts as special cases. The location-scale shift is intended to study a counterfactual policy aimed at changing not only the mean or location of a covariate but also its dispersion or scale.

arxiv-2208-07953.title: Opportunities for theory studies with public collider data
arxiv-2208-07953.creator: Matt Bellis, Brian Shuve, Anna Barth, Andrés Cook
arxiv-2208-07953.description: Abstract Over the last 20+ years, experimentalists have presented tantalizing hints of physics beyond the standard model, but nothing definitive. With the wealth of data from experiments, in particular the collider experiments, it is imperative that the community leave no reasonable model untested and no search unsought.

arxiv-2209-13294.title: Gamma-ray Pulsar Halos in the Galaxy
arxiv-2209-13294.creator: Kun Fang 1,∗
arxiv-2209-13294.description: Abstract Pulsar halos are extended gamma-ray structures generated by electrons and positrons escaping from pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe), considered a new class of gamma-ray sources. They are ideal indicators for cosmic-ray propagation in localized regions of the Galaxy and particle escape process from PWNe.

arxiv-2212-08791.title: Two-Scale Gradient Descent Ascent Dynamics Finds Mixed Nash Equilibria of Continuous Games: A Mean-Field Perspective
arxiv-2212-08791.creator: Yulong Lu
arxiv-2212-08791.description: Abstract . Finding the mixed Nash equilibria (MNE) of a two-player zero sum continuous game is an important and challenging problem in machine learning. A canonical algorithm to finding the MNE is the noisy gradient descent ascent method which in the infinite particle limit gives rise to the Mean-Field Gradient Descent Ascent (GDA) dynamics on the space of probability measures.

arxiv-2307-02422.title: Wishful Thinking is Risky Thinking Thanks: Department of Economics, Indiana University, Bloomington, IN 47408, USA. Email: {jburgh,emelo}@iu.edu . We are very grateful to Duarte Goncalves, Marco Acosta, Jack Berger, Collin Raymond, Ben Bushong, and participants at SAET 2023 and Georgia-Tech MWET 202
arxiv-2307-02422.creator: Jarrod Burgh Emerson Melo
arxiv-2307-02422.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jarrod Burgh Emerson Melo. We develop a model of wishful thinking that incorporates the costs and benefits of biased beliefs. We establish the connection between distorted beliefs and risk, revealing how wishful thinking can be understood in terms of risk measures. Our model accommodates extreme beliefs, allowing wishful-thinking decision-makers to assign zero probability to undesirable states and positive probability to otherwise impossible states. JEL classification: D01, D80, D84

Keywords:
wishful thinking, cognitive dissonance, risk, optimism, quantile maximization, preference for skewness

1.

arxiv-2307-15743.title: Micron-size spatial superpositions for the QGEM-protocol via screening and trapping
arxiv-2307-15743.creator: Martine Schut, Andrew Geraci, Sougato Bose, Anupam Mazumdar
arxiv-2307-15743.description: Abstract The quantum gravity-induced entanglement of masses (QGEM) protocol for testing quantum gravity using entanglement witnessing utilizes the creation of spatial quantum superpositions of two neutral, massive matter-wave interferometers kept adjacent to each other, separated by a distance d d .

arxiv-2402-09146.title: ResQuNNs:Towards Enabling Deep Learning in Quantum Convolution Neural Networks
arxiv-2402-09146.creator: Muhammad Kashif, Muhammad Shafique
arxiv-2402-09146.description: Abstract This paper focuses on methidenhances Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks (QuNNs) by introducing trainable quanvolutional layers and addressing the challenges in training deep QuNNs. Traditional QuNNs rely on static quanvolutional layers, limiting their feature extraction capabilities. Our approach enables the training of these layers, significantly improving the scalability and learning potential of QuNNs.

arxiv-2403-03022.title: Incommensurate broken helix induced by nonstoichiometry in the axion insulator candidate EuIn 2 As 2
arxiv-2403-03022.creator: Masaki Gen, Yukako Fujishiro, Kazuki Okigami, Satoru Hayami, Max T. Birch, Kiyohiro Adachi, Daisuke Hashizume, Takashi Kurumaji, Hajime Sagayama, Hironori Nakao, Yoshinori Tokura, Taka-hisa Arima
arxiv-2403-03022.description: Abstract Zintl phase EuIn 2 As 2 has garnered growing attention as an axion insulator candidate, triggered by the identification of a commensurate double- 𝐐 {\mathbf{Q}} broken-helix state in previous studies, however, its periodicity and symmetry remain subjects of debate.

arxiv-2408-13477.title: On the set of stable primes for postcritically infinite maps over number fields
arxiv-2408-13477.creator: Joachim König
arxiv-2408-13477.description: Abstract . Many interesting questions in arithmetic dynamics revolve, in one way or another, around the (local and/or global) reducibility behavior of iterates of a polynomial. We show that for very general families of integer polynomials f f (and, more generally, rational functions over number fields), the set of stable primes, i.e.

arxiv-2503-16933.title: Wold-type decomposition for Doubly commuting two-isometries
arxiv-2503-16933.creator: Monojit Bhattacharjee, Rajeev Gupta, Vidhya Venugopal
arxiv-2503-16933.description: Abstract . In this article, we prove that any pair of doubly commuting 2 2 -isometries on a Hilbert space has a Wold-type decomposition. Moreover, the analytic part of the pair is unitary equivalent to the pair of multiplication by coordinate function on a Dirichlet-type space on the bidisc.

arxiv-2504-10734.title: Uniqueness of Equilibrium Measure for a Family of Partially Hyperbolic Horseshoes
arxiv-2504-10734.creator: Krerley Oliveira, Marlon Oliveira, Eduardo Santana
arxiv-2504-10734.description: Abstract . In this paper, we show the uniqueness of equilibrium state for a family of partially hyperbolic horseshoes, introduced in [ 12 ] for some classes of continuous potentials. For the first class, the method used here is making use of the Sarig’s theory for countable shifts.

arxiv-2507-17097.title: On local rings of finite syzygy representation type
arxiv-2507-17097.creator: Souvik Dey, Kaito Kimura, Jian Liu, Yuya Otake
arxiv-2507-17097.description: Abstract . Let R R be a commutative Noetherian local ring. We give a characterization of when the completion of R R has an isolated singularity. This result simultaneously improves a theorem of Dao and Takahashi and a theorem of Bahlekeh, Hakimian, Salarian, and Takahashi.

arxiv-2601-15146.title: A Real-Time Error Prevention System for Gaze-Based Interaction in Virtual Reality Based on Anomaly Detection DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation email; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Huma
arxiv-2601-15146.creator: Björn R. Severitt, Yannick Sauer, Nora Castner, Siegfried Wahl
arxiv-2601-15146.description: Abstract . Gaze-based interaction enables intuitive, hands-free control in immersive environments, but remains susceptible to unintended inputs. We present a real-time error prevention system (EPS) that uses a temporal convolutional network autoencoder (TCNAE) to detect anomalies in gaze dynamics during selection tasks.

plos-pone-0003090.creator: Marta García-Lecea, Igor Kondrychyn, Steven H. Fong et al.

The choroid plexus (ChP), a component of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), produces the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and as a result plays a role in (i) protecting and nurturing the brain as well as (ii) in coordinating neuronal migration during neurodevelopment. plos-pone-0358561.title: PAK4-targeting PROTAC inhibits bladder cancer cell proliferation
plos-pone-0358561.creator: Shan Xu, Hongjun Xie, Zhao Yang, Zhenkun Ma, Xiaojing Bai, Xiaoyu Feng, Jiale An, Bohan Ma
plos-pone-0358561.description: PAK4-targeting PROTAC inhibits bladder cancer cell proliferation

pmc-10719698.title: Lncrna FGFR3-AS1 Is a Prognostic Indicator for Ovarian Cancer and Induces Cell Proliferation and Hinders Apoptosis
pmc-10719698.creator: Yuyang Zhang, Lili Sun, Tieshuang Chen, Yuanyuan Yue, Lin Zhao, Dan Zhang
pmc-10719698.description: Background:Ovarian cancer is one of the most common malignant tumors in Gynecology, whose treatment was seriously limited by the unclear understanding of molecular mechanism in disease development. LncRNA FGFR3-AS1 is involved in human cancers. In this study, we aimed to clarify its regulatory effect on ovarian cancer.

pmc-11462825.title: Genome-wide characterization of nitric oxide-induced NBS-LRR genes from Arabidopsis thaliana and their association in monocots and dicots
pmc-11462825.creator: Ashim Kumar Das, Adil Hussain, Nusrat Jahan Methela, Da-Sol Lee, Geum-Jin Lee, Youn-Ji Woo, Byung‑Wook Yun
pmc-11462825.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundNitric oxide (NO) is pivotal in regulating the activity of NBS-LRR specific R genes, crucial components of the plant’s immune system. It is noteworthy that previous research has not included a genome-wide analysis of NO-responsive NBS-LRR genes in plants.ResultsThe current study examined 29 NO-induced NBS-LRR genes from Arabidopsis thaliana, along with two monocots (rice and maize) and two dicots (soybean and tomato) using genome-wide analysis tools.

pmc-11478466.title: Performance of Soil Moisture Sensors at Different Salinity Levels: Comparative Analysis and Calibration
pmc-11478466.creator: Qiuju Qi, Hai Yang, Quanping Zhou, Xiaole Han, Zhengyang Jia, Yuehua Jiang, Zi Chen, Lili Hou, Shijia Mei, Zhou Shi, Manuel Aleixandre, Songchao Chen, Somsubhra Chakraborty, Wenjun Ji, Yongsheng Hong
pmc-11478466.description: Soil dielectric sensors have been widely used to obtain real-time soil moisture data, which are important for water resource management. However, soluble salts in the soil significantly affect the accuracy of these sensor measurements. Therefore, it is crucial to select suitable soil dielectric sensors for soil moisture measurements at different salinity levels.

pmc-11515507.title: SETDB1 targeting SESN2 regulates mitochondrial damage and oxidative stress in renal ischemia–reperfusion injury
pmc-11515507.creator: Kang Xia, Yumin Hui, Long Zhang, Qiangmin Qiu, Jiacheng Zhong, Hui Chen, Xiuheng Liu, Lei Wang, Zhiyuan Chen
pmc-11515507.description: BackgroundThe role of histone methyltransferase SETDB1 in renal ischemia–reperfusion (I/R) injury has not been explored yet. This study aims to investigate the potential mechanism of SETDB1 in regulating renal I/R injury and its impact on mitochondrial damage and oxidative stress.

pmc-12570299.title: Recurrent acute coronary syndrome caused by refractory vasospastic angina in a patient with essential thrombocythemia: a case report
pmc-12570299.creator: Masayoshi Fujii, Noritoshi Hiranuma, Yoshitaka Ohashi, Rita Pavasini, Andrea Erriquez, Suzit Bhusal, A Shaheer Ahmed, Deepti Ranganathan
pmc-12570299.description: BackgroundEssential thrombocythemia (ET) is a myeloproliferative disorder that increases the thrombotic risk and induces coronary spasms. Anagrelide, a common treatment for ET, has been suspected of trigger coronary spasm potentially leading to acute coronary syndrome (ACS).Case summaryA 51-year-old woman with ET who was treated with anagrelide developed recurrent ACS caused by refractory vasospastic angina.

pmc-12581512.title: Burden on the burdened: tuberculosis among Scheduled Tribes and non-Scheduled Tribes in constitutionally protected Scheduled and non-Scheduled areas of India
pmc-12581512.creator: Nishikant Singh, Sudheer Kumar Shukla, Ritam Dubey, Pratheeba John, Rituparna Sengupta, Ritesh Ranjan Pushkar, Navin Singh, Prince Chugh, Nishant Yadav, Rajeev Sadanandan
pmc-12581512.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIndia accounts for over a quarter of the global tuberculosis (TB) burden. Among the most affected are India’s Scheduled Tribes (STs) communities, experiencing a disproportionately higher TB prevalence compared to non-STs. Encouragingly, two successive rounds of National Family Health Survey (NFHS) showed the declined trend in overall TB prevalence in India, the rate of decline was markedly slower among STs, signalling that national gains have not translated into equitable progress.

pmc-12661616.title: Pain Cues in People With Dementia: Scoping Review
pmc-12661616.creator: Urška Smrke, Ana Milošič, Izidor Mlakar, Matic Kadiš, Satja Mulej Bratec, John Torous
pmc-12661616.description: BackgroundIndividuals with dementia, especially those in later stages, have difficulties with verbally reporting their experience of pain. This results in both underassessment and undertreatment of pain, signaling the need for better pain recognition in persons with dementia. A promising form of pain assessment is digital monitoring, which can concurrently and more objectively detect and use numerous relevant pain cues.

pmc-13064199.title: Draft genome sequences of nine marine-derived Dothideomycetes strains from Sugashima, Japan
pmc-13064199.creator: Kyoka A. Adachi, Yuri Fujita, Gohta Goshima, Gakuho Kurita
pmc-13064199.description: Marine-derived fungal species belonging to the class Dothideomycetes show remarkable variability in their life forms, such as obligate multicellularity and facultative multicellularity. The genetic basis of this diversity remains unknown. Here, we report the draft genome sequences of nine Dothideomycetes strains, including the genera Cladosporium, Neophaeotheca, Zalaria, and Neodevriesia, ranging from 19 to 36 Mb in size.

pmc-13295773.title: The Impact of Secure Attachment on Internet Altruistic Behavior: From the Helper and Seeker’s Perspective
pmc-13295773.creator: Lijuan Huang, Xianliang Zheng, Qingfeng Qiu
pmc-13295773.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Previous research on Internet altruistic behavior (IAB) has primarily focused on helpers. However, as a form of prosocial behavior embedded in online interpersonal interaction, IAB is likely shaped by characteristics of both helpers and seekers. Accordingly, the present research integrated attachment theory and social information processing models to examine how helper-related factors (secure attachment and positive empathy) and seeker-related factors (emoji symbols) influence IAB, as well as the mechanisms underlying these effects. Three studies were conducted.

pmc-13349058.title: Quality and consistency of genetic newborn screening reports in China: insights from a multi-laboratory analysis using simulated samples
pmc-13349058.creator: Jiaming Wu, Penghui Feng, Jinming Zhang, Honghui Zhou, Weijie Tian, Xingtong Chen, Chongyi Hao, Falin He
pmc-13349058.description: BackgroundChina currently lacks unified reporting standards for genetic newborn screening (gNBS), resulting in substantial variation in report content, structure, and variant interpretation across laboratories. This study aims to evaluate the quality of gNBS reports nationwide and provide practical evidence to support the development of standardized reporting guidelines.

pmc-13454310.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia among family members of affected children
pmc-13454310.creator: Can Ji, Jingyi Wang, Ping Zhang, Lijian Geng, Xueping Dong
pmc-13454310.description: This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) among family members of children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) and explore the relationships between these dimensions. A cross-sectional survey was conducted at Xuzhou First People’s Hospital (June-July 2025). A structured questionnaire collected demographic information and KAP data from 449 family caregivers.

pmc-13469783.title: A Bio‐Functional Mimetic Robot for Versatile Tasks From Cross‐Scale Manipulation to Limb‐Tool Integration
pmc-13469783.creator: Xin Tong, Tianle Zhang, Fei Mo, Qian Zhao, Zhongqing Sun, Yongkang Jiang, Yang Yang, Yingtian Li
pmc-13469783.description: Dexterous hands and robotic manipulators are essential physical interfaces for interacting with diverse environments. Traditional methods seek creature‐like dexterity through structural biomimicry of biological systems, a strategy that results in increased mechanical complexity and control challenges due to the stacking of components. This study presents the BioflexBot, a functionally biomimetic robot that moves beyond structural replication.

pmc-13503744.title: In silico study of 14-3-3σ and Nipah virus W proteins interaction
pmc-13503744.creator: Lia Griaznova, Vahram Arakelov, Grigor Arakelov, Karen Nazaryan

pmc-13602045.title: A brief acceptance and commitment therapy intervention for individuals at risk of neurodegenerative disease: A translational study in inherited prion disease
pmc-13602045.creator: Rhianna Brien, Lilian Dindo, Rachel Williams, Lucy Pauli, Beth Marsh, John Collinge, Simon Mead, Edgar Chan
pmc-13602045.description: Living at risk of a neurodegenerative condition such as inherited prion disease (IPD) is associated with substantial psychological burden, yet evidence-based supportive interventions are lacking. This unmet need is likely to grow as advances in biomarkers and predictive testing lead to increasing identification of individuals in pre-symptomatic stages of neurodegenerative disease.

pmc-13627589.title: Site-Specific Patterns of Distant Relapse on ^18F-FDG PET/Contrast-Enhanced CT According to Molecular Subtype in Breast Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13627589.creator: Agostino Chiaravalloti, Gianluca Vanni, Luca Verdesca, Daniele Di Biagio, Mario Tavolozza, Oreste Claudio Buonomo, Orazio Schillaci
pmc-13627589.description: PurposeTo describe the site-specific distribution of distant relapse detected by integrated ^18F-FDG PET/contrast-enhanced CT (PET/ceCT) in breast cancer patients and to explore its association with molecular subtype and clinicopathological features.MethodsThis retrospective study included 177 postoperative breast cancer patients who underwent PET/ceCT during follow-up/restaging for suspected recurrence.
